themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 23 this week compared to a 2.5-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks—an 820% increase (z-score: 12.36)—signaling either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapidly deteriorating enforcement in CD 314.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints filed this week vs. 2.5 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
820% spike with z-score of 12.36 (extreme statistical outlier)
Suggests concentrated problem in specific neighborhoods or corridors within CD 314
reporting_angles: Are specific blocks or transit corridors being targeted? Map the complaints geographically.
Interview Parks Dept and NYPD about enforcement response and whether this is gang-related or copycat tagging.

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Pile Up This Week
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 5 this week from a 0.5-per-week baseline—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—suggesting either a CitiBike system failure, theft surge, or litter enforcement gap.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints this week vs. 0.5 per-week average
Correlates with possible increase in bike thefts or system maintenance issues
reporting_angles: Contact CitiBike to determine if there's a docking station malfunction or service disruption in Midwood.
Check with 66th Precinct whether bike theft reports have also spiked in parallel.

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages Accelerate
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints climbed to 6 this week from a 2.8-per-week average—a 118% increase (z-score: 4.91)—indicating potential housing stock vulnerabilities in aging residential buildings where elevator failure traps elderly or disabled residents.
evidence: 6 elevator complaints filed this week vs. 2.8 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
Midwood is dense with mid-rise residential buildings built 1960s–1980s, likely aging infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings filed complaints and whether they share common maintenance contractors or building management companies.
Interview residents in affected buildings about wait times for repairs and impacts on elderly or mobility-limited tenants.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Campaign or Regulatory Gap
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 two weeks ago from a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 1500% increase (z-score: 11.62)—suggesting coordinated posting (political, commercial, or illicit) or a sudden enforcement gap.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
Pattern suggests either political campaign blitzing or organized commercial advertising push
reporting_angles: Map which intersections or transit nodes have the most postings—coordinate with Sanitation Dept.
Determine if postings are political (upcoming election?), commercial, or related to illicit activities.

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Spike Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints rose to 4 last week from a 0.6-per-week average—a 540% spike (z-score: 4.85)—possibly linked to construction activity (330 permits filed), nearby industrial sources, or weather conditions trapping pollutants.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints last week vs. 0.6 per-week average
330 DOB permits filed in past 90 days (247 alterations alone), suggesting active construction that may be dust/emissions source
reporting_angles: Cross-reference air quality complaint locations with DOB permit sites; interview residents near active construction.
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection about whether air monitors show elevated particulates in Midwood last week.
